about: B2B marketplaces: a buyer scans a supplier's product page (or, on some platforms, the supplier's own page). Safely reads the product page and the supplier's company pages, then shows one card per check and a risk score.
how_to_change: warning_points: how much a card adds to the score when it is a warning. Change the number, then deploy.
points_when_value: a different number for one exact card value (for example Account age 'Not provided').
enabled: false removes the card from every B2B scan and from the score.
platform_rules: add or remove a platform id in a list to change how those cards treat that platform.
A new card needs code once (something has to work out its result); after that its points and on/off live here.

no_founding_year_field.about: The platform has no founding-year field for any supplier, so 'Account age' does not blame the seller for a missing year (it is still a warning).

hidden_company_figures.about: The platform never shows sales or export figures (and may hide employees), so 'Company profile completeness' is not counted against the supplier.

no_order_details.about: Supplier directories that never show price, MOQ, Incoterms, packaging or delivery for any supplier, so 'Listing completeness' is not counted against the supplier.

prices_for_signed_in.about: Prices are shown only to signed-in buyers, so 'Price analysis' says it could not check the price instead of judging it.

supplier_page_scans.about: A buyer can scan the supplier's own page (many products) as well as a product page; product cards then say a supplier page was scanned.

platforms.name: ThomasNet
pages_read: company profile page (it is the listing)

platforms.name: Made-in-China
pages_read: product page or the supplier's shop home page

outside: web search for social pages and scam mentions (Serper)
Safely's own history and buyer reports

rules: Only contact details the supplier itself gives count: a phone, an email or a website. The platform's message form is not a contact channel.
Paid membership levels (Gold, Diamond, Premium...) are never counted as a check on the company.
The year a supplier joined the platform is not the year the company was founded.
Missing price, MOQ or shipping terms is normal in B2B and is not suspicious on its own.
A judgement belongs to the company, not to one product page.

cards.what_it_checks: The page is on the platform's real domain, not a lookalike.
Scam reports from Safely users and earlier scans of this supplier.
The supplier's own website: given by the supplier, or found by web search (marked as not given).
Does this look like a real, operating business (no made-up, impossible or self-contradicting details, no random mix of industries)?
Name, founding year, size and products hang together.
The listing describes a real, specific product (specs, materials), not generic copy-paste text.
The price and minimum order are plausible for the product.
The supplier gives at least one direct channel: phone, email or website.
Pressure tactics: 'deal expires today', 'decide now', discouraging samples or checks.
100% payment before shipment, or untraceable payment (Western Union, crypto, gift cards, a personal account).
The photos look like the supplier's own, not stock or reused images.
Shown only for licence-only products (botox, fillers, prescription medicines) or a false manufacturer claim.
The platform's own check on the company (verified badge, audit, licence check); paid levels are not a check.
How old the company says it is; a missing year is a small warning.
reads: the company's own text about years in business

cards.what_it_checks: The platform's own figures: orders, rating, on-time and reorder rate.
Products that are common bait in fake commodity deals, or a range that does not fit the company.
Certificates the company shows.
Says when the company's own page could not be loaded, so some details may be missing.
Employees, sales and export share filled in.
How many of the 9 order details are given (price, MOQ, payment, port, capacity, delivery, Incoterms, packaging...).
The company's pages on Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, Trustpilot, reviews; scam mentions online.
